sources.entry: py-spy - A sampling profiler for Python programs. Written in Rust.

summary.one_liner: py-spy is a low-overhead sampling profiler for CPython programs, written in Rust, that attaches to a running process by PID or launches a script, without modifying the program's code.
summary.what_it_does: py-spy reads the memory of a running Python process to reconstruct its call stacks, so it does not run inside the profiled program. The record subcommand samples a process and writes a flame graph (SVG), speedscope profile, or raw data, with options for sampling rate, GIL-only filtering, native extension profiling, thread IDs, and subprocesses. The top subcommand shows a live, top-style view of which functions consume the most time. The dump subcommand prints the current call stack of each Python thread, optionally with local variables, which is useful for finding where a program is hung. The README says it supports Linux, macOS, Windows and FreeBSD and CPython versions 2.3-2.7 and 3.3-3.15. Idle-thread detection and a --nonblocking mode that avoids pausing the target are also described.
use_cases: profile a slow Python program without changing its code
find where a production Python service spends CPU time
generate a flame graph of a Python process
diagnose a hung Python process by dumping thread stacks
live view of hot functions in a running Python program
profile multiprocessing or gunicorn worker subprocesses
notable: Samples from outside the process, so it is safe for production use per the README
Works without restarting the program or modifying its code
Record, top, and dump subcommands cover flame graphs, live views, and stack snapshots
Can profile native C/C++/Cython extensions with --native on supported platforms
Installable from PyPI as prebuilt wheels
caveats: Attaching to an existing PID usually requires root on Linux, and macOS always requires root; Docker and Kubernetes need SYS_PTRACE capability
macOS System Integrity Protection blocks profiling of the system /usr/bin/python
Native extension profiling is only available on some platforms and architectures; 32-bit Windows, PyPy, and UCS2 Python 2 are not supported
Idle-thread detection is heuristic and can produce false positives; --nonblocking can yield occasional errors or partial stacks
keywords: where is my python program spending time
